en: Thus have I heard: the *Kukkuravatikasutta*, the fifty-seventh discourse of the *Majjhima Nikāya*.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Koliyans at a town of the Koliyans named Haliddavasana.
Then Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans, a cow-vow ascetic, and Seniya, the naked dog-vow ascetic, approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans, the cow-vow ascetic, paid homage to the Blessed One.
He sat down to one side. But the naked Seniya, the dog-duty practitioner, exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, he curled up like a dog and sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans, the ox-duty practitioner, said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, this naked ascetic Seniya, who practices the dog-duty, is a performer of difficult deeds; he eats food dropped on the ground.
For a long time he has fully undertaken and observed that dog-duty.
What is his destination, what is his future state?”
“Enough, Puṇṇa! Let this be; do not ask me this.
A second time, Puṇṇa the Koliyan son, the cowherd...
[as before] ...and a third time, Puṇṇa the Koliyan son, the cowherd, said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, this naked ascetic Seniya, who follows the dog-vow and practices austerities, eats food placed on the bare ground.
He has long since fully undertaken and observed that dog-vow.
What is his destination, what is his future state?”
“Certainly, Puṇṇa, I do not get you.
Enough, Puṇṇa, let this be; do not ask me this.
Nevertheless, I shall answer you.”
In this case, Puṇṇa, a certain person develops the dog-vow, complete and uninterrupted;
he develops the dog-conduct, complete and uninterrupted; he develops the dog-mind, complete and uninterrupted; he develops the dog-appearance, complete and uninterrupted.
Having thus developed the dog-vow, perfect and unbroken; having developed the dog-ethic, perfect and unbroken; having developed the dog-mind, perfect and unbroken;
and having developed the dog-like appearance, perfect and unbroken, with the breakup of the body, after death, he reappears in the company of dogs.
But if he holds such a view as this: “By means of this virtue, or vow, or austerity, or holy life, I shall become a god or some other kind of deity,” that is his wrong view.
For one with wrong view, Puṇṇa, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm.
Thus, Puṇṇa, the dog-vow, when successful, leads to companionship with dogs; when unsuccessful, it leads to hell.
When this was said, the naked ascetic Seniya, the follower of the dog-duty, wept and shed tears.
Then the Blessed One said to Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans, the cow-duty practitioner:
"I did not obtain this from you, Puṇṇa."
“Enough, Puṇṇa, let this be; do not ask me this.
“I am not weeping, Bhante, because the Blessed One has said this to me;
rather, Bhante, this dog-vow has been fully undertaken and observed by me for a long time.”
"Venerable sir, this Puṇṇa, son of the Koliyans, is a cow-vow observer.
For a long time he has fully undertaken and observed that cow-vow.
What is his destination, what is his future state?"
“Enough, Seniya! Let this be; do not ask me this.
A second time, the naked ascetic Seniya … and a third time, the naked ascetic Seniya, a follower of the dog-vow, said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, this Puṇṇa, son of the Koliyans, is an ox-vow observer.
He has long practiced and undertaken that ox-vow.
What is his destination, what is his future state?”
“Certainly, Seniya, I do not get you.
Enough, Seniya, let this be; do not ask me this.
Nevertheless, I shall answer you.”

In this case, Seniya, a certain person develops the cow’s way of life, perfect and uninterrupted; he develops the cow’s virtue, perfect and uninterrupted; he develops the cow’s mind, perfect and uninterrupted;
he develops the cow’s practice, perfect and uninterrupted. Having developed the cow’s way of life, perfect and uninterrupted;
having developed the cow’s virtue, perfect and uninterrupted; having developed the cow’s mind, perfect and uninterrupted; having developed the cow’s practice, perfect and uninterrupted...
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of cattle.
But if he holds such a view as this: "By this virtue, or vow, or austerity, or holy life, I shall become a god or some other kind of deity," that is his wrong view.
Seniya, for one with wrong view, I declare there are two destinations: either hell or the animal realm.
"Thus, Seniya, when practiced correctly, the cow-vow leads to companionship with cows; when practiced incorrectly, it leads to hell.
When this was said, Puṇṇa the Koliyan, the cow-vow practitioner, wept and shed tears.
Then the Blessed One said this to the naked Seniya, the dog-vow practitioner:
“I could not convince you of this, Seniya.
Enough, Seniya, let it be; do not ask me this.
“Venerable sir, I am not weeping because the Blessed One has spoken thus to me; rather, I am weeping because I have failed to gain the approval of such a superior person as the Blessed One.”
"Moreover, Bhante, this cow-vow has been undertaken and observed by me for a long time.
With such confidence as I have in the Blessed One, Bhante,
the Blessed One is capable of teaching the Dhamma in such a way that both I might abandon this cow-vow and this naked Seniya, who practices the dog-vow, might abandon that dog-vow."
“In that case, Puṇṇa, listen and pay close attention; I shall speak.
“Yes, venerable sir,” Puṇṇa, the son of the Koliyans, a cowherd, replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Puṇṇa, there are these four kinds of kamma that have been realized by me through direct higher knowledge and declared.
What are the four?
There is, Puṇṇa, dark kamma with dark result;”
There is, Puṇṇa, black action with black result; there is, Puṇṇa, white action with white result;
there is, Puṇṇa, action that is neither black nor white with neither black nor white result, which leads to the destruction of action.
And what, Puṇṇa, is dark kamma with dark result?
Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person performs a bodily formation that is afflictive, performs a verbal formation that is afflictive, and performs a mental formation that is afflictive.
Having performed an afflictive bodily formation, having performed an afflictive verbal formation, and having performed an afflictive mental formation, he reappears in an afflictive world.
When he has been reborn in a world that is afflicted, afflicted contacts touch him.
Being touched by afflicted contacts, he experiences afflicted feeling, which is exclusively painful, just like beings in hell.
Thus, Puṇṇa, the arising of one being occurs from another being.
Whatever one does, by that one is reborn;
once reborn, contacts touch one.
Thus, Puṇṇa, I say that beings are heirs to their own karma.
This, Puṇṇa, is called black action with black result.
And what, Puṇṇa, is white action with white result?
Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person performs a wholesome bodily formation, performs a wholesome verbal formation, and performs a wholesome mental formation.

Having performed a non-afflictive bodily formation, having performed a non-afflictive verbal formation, and having performed a non-afflictive mental formation, one is reborn in a non-afflictive world.
Being reborn in that non-afflictive world, non-afflictive contacts touch him.
Being touched by those non-afflictive contacts, he experiences a non-afflictive feeling that is exclusively pleasant, just like the Subhakiṇha devas.
"Thus, Puṇṇa, there is the arising of a being from a being;
one is reborn according to what one does,
and once reborn, contacts touch that person."
Thus, Puṇṇa, I say that beings are heirs to their own kamma.
This, Puṇṇa, is called white kamma with white result.
And what, Puṇṇa, is black-and-white kamma with black-and-white result?
Here, Puṇṇa, a certain person performs a bodily formation that is both harmful and harmless;
he performs a verbal formation that is both harmful and harmless; he performs a mental formation that is both harmful and harmless.
Having performed a bodily formation that is both harmful and harmless, and [having performed] a verbal formation... that is both harmful and harmless—
Having formed a verbal formation, and having formed a mental formation that is either afflictive or non-afflictive,
one is reborn in a world that is either afflictive or non-afflictive.
Having been reborn in a world that is either afflictive or non-afflictive, both afflictive and non-afflictive contacts touch that person.

Thus, being touched by both afflictive and non-afflictive contacts, one experiences both afflictive and non-afflictive feelings, mixed with pleasure and pain—just as humans, some gods, and some beings in the states of deprivation do.
In this way, Puṇṇa, the arising of a being occurs from a being; one is reborn according to what one has done.
“Contact touches him accordingly.
It is in this way, Puṇṇa, that I say beings are heirs to their own kamma.
This, Puṇṇa, is called kamma that is dark-and-bright with dark-and-bright result.”
And what, Puṇṇa, is the action that is neither dark nor bright, with neither-dark-nor-bright result, which leads to the exhaustion of action?
Here, Puṇṇa, it is the volition for the abandoning of that action which is dark with dark result;
the volition for the abandoning of that action which is bright with bright result; and the volition for the abandoning of that action which is both dark and bright with both dark and bright result.
“The volition for its abandonment—
this, Puṇṇa, is called action that is neither dark nor bright with neither-dark-nor-bright result, which leads to the destruction of action.
These, Puṇṇa, are the four kinds of action that I have realized through direct knowledge and proclaimed.”
When this was said, Puṇṇa, the Koliyan son, a cowherd, said this to the Blessed One:
“Magnificent, Bhante! Magnificent, Bhante!
Just as, Bhante, ... [as before] ...”
“May the Blessed One accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.
But the naked Seniya, the dog-duty practitioner, said this to the Blessed One:
“Magnificent, Bhante! Magnificent, Bhante!”
"Just as, venerable sir... [as before] ...has been made clear.
Venerable sir, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
May I receive the going-forth in the presence of the Blessed One, venerable sir; may I receive the full ordination."
“Seniya, whoever who was formerly a member of another sect desires the going-forth in this Dhamma and Discipline,
desires the full admission, must undergo a four-month probation. At the end of those four months, if the bhikkhus are satisfied with his mind,
they grant him the going-forth and the full admission to the state of a bhikkhu.”
"Moreover, I recognize the distinction between individuals here.
"Venerable sir, if those who were formerly members of other sects desire the going-forth and desire the full ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, they undergo a four-month probation;
at the end of the four months, if the bhikkhus are satisfied with them..."

“They grant the going-forth and ordain one for the state of a bhikkhu; I shall undergo the probation for four years, and at the end of those four years, if the bhikkhus are pleased with me, let them grant me the going-forth and ordain me for the state of a bhikkhu.
Then the naked ascetic Seniya, the dog-duty practitioner, received the going-forth in the presence of the Blessed One; he received ordination.
Not long after his full ordination, the Venerable Seniya, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute,

soon realized for himself through direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed goal of the holy life, for the sake of which young men of good family rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness; having attained it, he dwelt therein.
“He has understood: ‘Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.
And so the Venerable Seniya became one of the Arahants.
The *Kukkuravatika Sutta* is finished; it is the seventh.
